predecessors.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
predecessors.text: Orientale Province: 'On 12 December 1960, Gizenga declared his new government, the Free Republic of the Congo,' 'based in Orientale Province'

successors.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
successors.text: Orientale, Bukavu, northern Kivu, Sankuru and Maniema: 'not fully reintegrated into the Republic of the Congo until Gizenga was arrested in January 1962'

ledger.x: 1960: Antoine Gizenga declares the Free Republic of the Congo at Stanleyville.
24 December 1960: 'Stanleyville troops occupied Bukavu and arrested the local army commander.'
January 1961: 'Gizenga's authority was also established over the Sankuru District of Kasai Province.'
By 10 January 1961 'control had been consolidated in Goma and the northern Kivu region.'
By 10 January 1961 'Stanleyville forces had occupied northern Katanga as far in as Manono' without resistance.
October 1961: 'Pro-Gizenga administrators were installed in the Maniema and Sankuru districts.'
January 1962: Gizenga is censured by Parliament on 15 January and flown to Léopoldville on 20 January; the infobox gives 'Disestablished: 16 January 1962'.
January 1962: the page is silent on what became of the northern Katanga strip when the Stanleyville regime ended; it falls back to the Katanga claim until January 1963.
January 1962: the Free Republic ends with Gizenga's arrest; its land passes to the Republic of the Congo (identity.successors).

wars.name: Congo Crisis (Stanleyville government)
wars.outcome: The regime ended politically, not by conquest, in January 1962: Gizenga joined Adoula's coalition on 2 August 1961, returned to Stanleyville in September, was stripped of the vice premiership on 15 January 1962 and imprisoned at Camp Kokolo on 25 January.

certainty.note: Control was by garrisons and administrators, not a frontier: the page gives provinces and districts (Orientale, northern Kivu, Sankuru, Maniema) and 'as far in as Manono', with no map.
